# Customer Churn & Retention Analysis

An end-to-end analytics project to understand customer churn, retention, customer value, and win-back opportunities using Excel data, Python/Pandas, MySQL, and Power BI.

### Dashboard Preview

![Customer Churn & Retention Power BI dashboard preview](data:image/png;base64,)

## Project Goal

Help a Retention or Marketing Manager identify churn patterns, monitor customer risk, and prioritize high-value customers for win-back campaigns.

## Data & Workflow

The project combines customer, order, delivery, and marketing campaign data. Python and Pandas are used for cleaning and customer-level analysis; MySQL supports structured SQL analysis; Power BI presents the results in an interactive dashboard.

## Business Rules

- Only orders with `order_status = "Delivered"` count as valid purchases.
- A customer is **Churned** after more than 90 days without a valid purchase. Customers with no valid purchases are **Never Purchased**, not churned.
- Risk segments use recency: **Low** (<30 days), **Medium** (30–59 days), **High** (60+ days), for customers who have purchased.
- Historical CLV is observed historical net revenue (`order_value + shipping_fee`), not a forecast. The analysis date is the latest valid purchase date in the dataset.

## Dashboard Highlights

The Power BI Executive Overview includes customer and churn KPIs, customer status and risk, churn by acquisition channel and region, retention metrics, historical value at risk, slicers, and a prioritized win-back customer table. Use the actual dataset and validated measures when interpreting the report values.
